status_summary: NSPM-1 (2025-01-20) organized the National Security Council system and describes the NSC as the President's principal means of coordinating national security policy, strategies and long-term planning, but it does not address the National Defense Strategy, war plans, force allocation or officer promotions. A new National Security Strategy was released on 2025-12-04 and a National Defense Strategy on 2026-01-23, and the public descriptions reviewed do not say that the NSC led their drafting or that the NSC and OMB reviewed the defense strategy, war plans or force allocation. On promotions, the White House acknowledged on 2025-07-30 that the President personally meets candidates for four-star posts, a practice an Associated Press report attributed to the Defense Secretary, which is a White House review of the most senior nominees rather than an NSC review of all general and flag officer promotions. A Congressional Research Service product of 2026-07-17 describes promotion lists as going from the Secretary of Defense to the President and does not mention NSC review.

timeline.event: NSPM-1 organized the National Security Council system, describing the NSC as the President's principal means of coordinating national security policy, strategies and long-term planning; it does not address the National Defense Strategy, war plans, force allocation or officer promotions.

The White House acknowledged that the President meets with candidates nominated for four-star general and admiral posts, a practice the report said began at the Defense Secretary's initiative; the NSC is not mentioned.
The administration released its 2025 National Security Strategy.
The Department of War released the 2026 National Defense Strategy.

A CRS Insight on officer promotions described the statutory path of promotion lists (Secretary of Defense to the President) and congressional concern about personnel actions toward general and flag officers; it did not mention NSC review.

title: NSC to lead review of formal strategies, war plans and general and flag officer promotions
uncertainties: Not found: any report that the NSC itself reviews general and flag officer promotion lists; the presidential meetings cover four-star candidates only, and reported removals of officers from promotion lists were described as actions of the Defense Secretary, not the NSC. NSPM-1 was read through a summarizing fetch rather than as full text, and only NSPM-1, NSPM-2 and NSPM-12 were checked among the national security memoranda. The public strategy summaries do not say who drafted them, and the 2026 National Defense Strategy document itself was not opened. Absence of public evidence is not evidence of absence, since NSC process is largely internal. The progress figure is an inference. Staffing is covered by c02-03 and cuts to general officer numbers by c04-09.
